title: Low-degree open direct-image sequence for adic Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Let $X_0$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type $k_0$-scheme smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] with their underlying constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], and ordinary and derived direct images [def-wf-middle-extension, def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-common-stage-derived-direct-image]. For any short exact sequence $0\to G_1\to G\to G_2\to0$ of lisse such sheaves [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], there is a natural exact sequence of constructible Weil sheaves
$$0\to j_*G_1\to j_*G\to j_*G_2\xrightarrow{\delta}R^1j_*G_1.$$
Here $R^1j_*G_1=\mathcal H^1(Rj_*G_1)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. All its maps, including $\delta$, are Weil-equivariant. Moreover $R^rj_*G_i=0$ for $r<0$, $R^0j_*G_i=j_*G_i$, $j^*j_*G_i\simeq G_i$, and $j^*R^1j_*G_i=0$. These identifications and the displayed exact sequence commute with restriction to open subschemes of $X_0$. No purity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05TE, lemma-right-derived-delta-functor, and the left-exact low-degree sequence immediately preceding it; adic/Weil version required by main-20261015 p-dl-a1-exact.proof.md Step 1 and treated at the coefficient stages of Bhatt–Scholze §6.8. This is the adic enhancement, not a claim that Tag 05TE itself supplies adic coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and use the same letter $j$ for the geometric open immersion. These are smooth separated finite-type curves over the perfect field $k$. Finite type over a field makes them Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field has only the two ideals), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Thus the rational/common-stage categories used in the statement are defined. In particular all their opens are quasi-compact. Forget the Weil structures in the given sequence. It is short exact in the underlying constructible heart by [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact]. Apply clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] in this heart to obtain a distinguished triangle $G_1\to G\to G_2\xrightarrow{w}G_1[1]$ in the geometric constructible category. This use of the heart does not put a triangulated structure on Frobenius-fixed pairs.

source.place: Step 1: underlying geometric short exact sequence and its triangle.

proof.text: The actual adic $Rj_*$ is an exact triangulated functor on these geometric categories. To check the coefficient issue, at a finite field $E$ first work over the completed sheaves $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,U}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. The natural comparison of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies ordinary completed-ring derived direct image with the strict reduction-tower/derived-limit construction in the direct-image definition [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Ordinary total right derived direct image is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Its constructible restriction exists by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible], since $j$ is a morphism of finite-type schemes over $k$ and $\ell$ is invertible. Its triangles are the inherited ambient triangles by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Since $U$ and $X$ are Noetherian and finite-dimensional (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies this derived-complete integral category with the integral category underlying the rational categories of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]; so that theorem gives the exact rational functor. The coherent direct-image comparisons with finite field extension in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] satisfy the unit, associator and shift equations, so [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] descends the family of these exact functors to an exact functor on the pair category, which is the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] built on the same finite stages; its triangles are the images of finite-stage triangles. Hence applying it to the triangle of step 1 gives a distinguished triangle $Rj_*G_1\to Rj_*G\to Rj_*G_2\to Rj_*G_1[1]$, with bounded constructible terms.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; completed-coefficient comparison specified by the cited DAG tool.

proof.text: Apply the bottom-cohomology assertion of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] with $m=0$ to each of $G_1,G,G_2$. Each is a lisse sheaf placed in degree zero on the dense open of the smooth separated finite-type curve. It gives $\mathcal H^r(Rj_*G_i)=0$ for $r<0$ and the natural augmentation identification $\mathcal H^0(Rj_*G_i)\cong j_*G_i$. The same assertion gives $j^*j_*G_i\cong G_i$. These are statements at rational/common-stage coefficients, rather than an application of a finite-torsion comparison without change of coefficients.

source.place: Tag 05TD, lemma-left-exact-higher-derived (1),(3); its rational/common-stage version is the cited existing node.

proof.text: Use clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] on the image triangle of step 2. Its cohomology sequence is exact in the constructible heart. Step 3 kills the degree $-1$ term and identifies its degree-zero terms, giving precisely $0\to j_*G_1\to j_*G\to j_*G_2\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathcal H^1(Rj_*G_1)$. Explicitly $\delta$ is $\mathcal H^0(Rj_*w)$ followed by the shift comparison $\mathcal H^0((Rj_*G_1)[1])\cong\mathcal H^1(Rj_*G_1)$. This fixes the boundary and its sign. It is natural in the short exact sequence: a morphism of such sequences extends to a morphism of their heart triangles. Indeed the triangle axiom supplies the third map after the first two; because the third object is the cokernel of the first map in the heart, that map must be the given map on $G_2$. Applying $Rj_*$ and cohomology gives the commuting boundary square.

source.place: Tag 05TE, lemma-right-derived-delta-functor; the low-degree sequence preceding it. Heart formulation: BBD 1.3.3–1.3.6.

proof.text: The Frobenius pullbacks on $U$ and $X$ commute with ordinary cohomology and the heart identifications by [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. Pull back the short exact sequence by geometric Frobenius and then apply its three Weil isomorphisms. This is a morphism of short exact sequences. The naturality argument of step 4 therefore makes $w$ commute with these isomorphisms. The canonical equivariant direct-image comparison of [lem-fix-weil-operations] carries this to a commuting square for $Rj_*w$. Taking $\mathcal H^0$ and the shift comparison gives $\delta\circ\theta_{j_*G_2}=\theta_{R^1j_*G_1}\circ g_X^*\delta$. Thus $\delta$ is a Weil-sheaf morphism. The same argument, or functoriality on the first two arrows, proves equivariance of all the other maps; the bottom-cohomology and open-counit identifications commute with the Weil structures by the cited cohomology node. Exactness is tested on the underlying heart by [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact], so the resulting sequence is exact as a sequence of constructible Weil sheaves.

source.place: Step 1: Weil equivariance of the connecting map, obtained by naturality on geometric triangles.

proof.text: Let $a:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be any open, put $U_W=U_0\times_{X_0}W_0$, and write $b:U_W\hookrightarrow U_0$ and $j_W:U_W\hookrightarrow W_0$. At a finite coefficient field $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] identifies the rationalized adic functors and their adjunctions with the ambient continuous-$E$ module functors. For these functors clause (2) of [lem-sfb-derived-direct-image-open-coherence], with $f=j$ and open $a$, gives the natural isomorphism $a^*Rj_*\cong Rj_{W,*}b^*$. Its normalization is the sectionwise identity on a K-injective representative, $I(V\times_X U)$, and clause (3) gives compatibility with successive restrictions. Transport this isomorphism back by the realization equivalences. The comparison is the open unit-square-counit exchange: both maps on the representative are this same identity. [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] therefore makes these isomorphisms compatible with finite coefficient extensions, since it preserves that specified exchange. By the clause of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] on compatible natural transformations, they consequently descend to a natural isomorphism on the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the same successive-restriction identity. All opens here are quasi-compact by step 1, so the open-coherence theorem applies even when $W_0$ is empty or meets only some components.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open. Rational realization: Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Restriction is exact on coefficient module sheaves by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; hence it commutes with kernels, images, cokernels and the cohomology of complexes. Under the rational/common-stage cohomology identification with ordinary pro-etale module representatives in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], the comparison of step 6 therefore gives $a^*R^rj_*G_i\cong R^rj_{W,*}b^*G_i$ and $a^*j_*G_i\cong j_{W,*}b^*G_i$. The latter also follows directly from the section formula of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Exact restriction sends the short exact input to its restricted input, and sends its heart triangle to that triangle: the connecting arrow is characterized by clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Apply the natural comparison of step 6 to this triangle. Taking cohomology shows that the comparison square commutes for $\mathcal H^0(Rj_*w)$, and hence for $\delta$ after the shift identification. Thus the entire displayed sequence and its identifications commute with open restriction, including successive restrictions. Since the opens are defined over $k_0$, the exchange is equivariant by [lem-fix-weil-operations].

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; derived boundary compatibility by its naturality on triangles.

proof.text: Take $W_0=U_0$ in step 6. Then $U_W=U_0$ and $j_W=\operatorname{id}_{U_0}$, so $j^*Rj_*G_i\cong G_i$. Indeed the ordinary identity functor applied to any complex is that complex, so its derived functor is the identity. By the cohomology-restriction identifications of step 7, $j^*R^1j_*G_i\cong\mathcal H^1(G_i)=0$, since $G_i$ is in the heart. In degree zero this is the already specified counit $j^*j_*G_i\cong G_i$, because the comparison on sections is the identity. The same representative computation shows that the negative-degree zero identifications and all the degree-zero identifications restrict as claimed. No weight or purity property has entered any step.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q136-821d188d3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every proof step and the statement of every cited node. Sources checked: blueprint main-20261015 p-dl-a1-exact Steps 1–2; Stacks derived.tex 05TD and 05TE; sites-cohomology.tex 0D6G and 08FI. The statement is unchanged and true: tested with j=id, empty X, A^1 minus a point (delta can be nonzero) and disconnected X. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are correct and their hypotheses hold (Noetherian, finite-dimensional, perfect field, smooth pure dimension-one curve, quasi-compact opens). Step 4's naturality argument (TR3 plus the cokernel) and step 5's Frobenius equivariance (uniqueness of the boundary, the Weil structure on Rj_* from lem-fix-weil-operations) are complete. There are no new nodes and no cycle. Two citations were missing (C4, E6) and I repaired both in the fixed item file. (1) Step 2 applied prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport, which is stated for def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, to the def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed category without citing lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization, which identifies the two. (2) Steps 2 and 6 descended the exact functor and the natural isomorphisms to the common-stage Qlbar category using only def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients; they now cite prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors. proof_deps and tool_uses are updated. Neither is a statement or proof step of the trace formula or Poincare duality. Except lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence, an adjunction-coherence lemma, all of them are already in the closure of the pre-existing statement dependency rem-dl-a1-conventions, and my two added citations reach nothing new.
